product_family: Adobe Podcast is a web-based AI audio recording, transcription, editing, and enhancement tool available as a standalone freemium product ($0 free, $9.99/month premium) and included with Creative Cloud subscriptions. Features include Enhance Speech, transcription, Studio for remote recording, and Generative Fill with custom voice models.

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type II (Security, Availability, Confidentiality)
certifications.proof_quote: Adobe Creative Cloud for enterprise holds SOC 2 Type II certification, but Adobe Podcast is not explicitly listed in the certified products scope (Photoshop, InDesign, Adobe Express, etc.). No public evidence Adobe Podcast itself is SOC 2 certified.

certifications.name: ISO 27001:2022
certifications.proof_quote: Adobe Creative Cloud for enterprise holds ISO 27001:2022 certification. Adobe Podcast is not explicitly listed in the certified products. No public evidence of Adobe Podcast specific ISO 27001 certification.

certifications.name: GDPR Compliance
certifications.proof_quote: GDPR is a legal framework Adobe complies with company-wide. Adobe publishes a GDPR program and offers a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) covering products where Adobe acts as processor of customer personal data. This is verified at the Adobe corporate level; there is no Adobe Podcast-specific GDPR attestation, so coverage is inherited from Adobe's general GDPR/DPA framework rather than a product-specific statement. Not a verbatim vendor quote from a Podcast-scoped page.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of HIPAA compliance or certification for Adobe Podcast. While Adobe Creative Cloud for enterprise is HIPAA-ready, Adobe Podcast is not listed in HIPAA-certified product scope.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: Adobe Creative Cloud for enterprise supports FedRAMP Tailored certification for some products, but Adobe Podcast is not listed as FedRAMP certified.

privacy.ai_training_note: Per Adobe's Content Analysis FAQ, Adobe may analyze content processed or stored on its servers using machine learning to improve products and services, aggregated first; users can opt out at account.adobe.com/privacy under 'Content analysis for product improvement.' Adobe states it does not analyze customer content to train generative AI models, and that Firefly and partner models do not train on customer content (exception: content submitted to Adobe Stock). Adobe Podcast is not separately addressed in Adobe's published content-analysis or training documentation, so its posture is inherited from Adobe's general policy rather than a Podcast-specific statement. The earlier claim that free/consumer tiers 'train AI models on anonymized audio' traced only to a third-party blog and conflates product-improvement content analysis with generative-model training, which Adobe explicitly disclaims. The Generative Fill feature lets a user train a custom voice model on their own recording, a user-initiated product feature distinct from Adobe training its own models.

products.name: Adobe Podcast (Free)
products.data_scope: Audio files, transcripts, user account data
products.notes: 30-minute file limit, 1-hour daily enhancement cap, Studio limited to 30-minute projects (2 per day), no access to original recordings. May train on anonymized data with opt-out available.

products.name: Adobe Podcast (Premium)
products.data_scope: Audio files (up to 1GB), video files (MP4/MOV), transcripts, user account data
products.notes: $9.99/month or $99.99/year. 4-hour daily enhancement limit, bulk uploads, unlimited Studio downloads, speaker-separated recordings. Enterprise users can configure DPA and GDPR controls.

products.name: Adobe Podcast Studio
products.data_scope: Multi-participant audio streams, continuous session data
products.notes: Each participant's audio captured directly in their browser, continuously saved throughout session. Protects against connection drops.

products.name: Adobe Podcast Generative Fill
products.data_scope: User audio, custom voice model data
products.notes: Pro feature allowing users to train custom voice models to patch recording mistakes. Users have control over model training.

compare.pricing_model: Freemium (free tier with limitations; $9.99/month or $99.99/year premium). Also included with Creative Cloud subscriptions at no additional cost.
compare.data_residency: Adobe secure cloud (region not specified in public docs)

flags: OVER-CLAIM RISK: Adobe marketing may imply SOC 2 and ISO 27001 apply to Adobe Podcast (since the product is part of Adobe and Adobe Creative Cloud is certified), but Adobe Podcast is NOT explicitly listed in the certified products scope. Buyers should verify with Adobe sales whether their specific use case is covered.

NO DEDICATED TRUST CENTER: Adobe Podcast has no dedicated trust/security/compliance page. All compliance and privacy documentation is inherited from Adobe's main privacy policy and terms, creating potential confusion for enterprise buyers about what specifically applies.

AI CONTENT ANALYSIS (OPT-OUT): Per Adobe's Content Analysis FAQ, Adobe may analyze content with machine learning to improve products and services by default, with an opt-out at account.adobe.com/privacy. Adobe states it does not train generative AI models on customer content. Adobe Podcast is not separately addressed, so this posture is inherited from Adobe's general policy; enterprise buyers should confirm scope via a DPA. Do not repeat the third-party-blog claim that Adobe trains its models on free-tier audio, which contradicts Adobe's own documentation.

HIPAA NOT CONFIRMED: Adobe Creative Cloud for enterprise is HIPAA-ready, but Adobe Podcast is not listed in HIPAA scope. Healthcare organizations should not assume HIPAA compliance without explicit vendor confirmation.

GROWTH-STAGE PRODUCT: Adobe Podcast is a newer AI-driven consumer/freemium product, not a mature enterprise product with formal audit reports like Adobe Document Cloud or Experience Cloud. Compliance certifications may not be in scope.
IDENTITY CONFIRMED: Adobe Podcast (podcast.adobe.com) is definitely an Adobe product, not a third-party tool with a similar name.
